title: CLO 2025 Academic Month: The Path of 3D Innovation from Concept to Implementation
description: CLO 2025 Official Academic Monthly Course Review Released! Tong Jiale from Jiangsu Guotai Guosheng Group shares the changes brought by 3D technology to the traditional fashion industry and the company's experience in the process of 3D transformation.
transcript:
How did you come up with the idea of promoting 3D virtual technology?  
I have been developing virtual 3D technology for a long time.  
It has been a long time since then.  
Today, I would like to talk about how to promote 3D virtual technology  
and how to promote 3D technology within the supply chain industry and within the brand.  

First of all, from the McKinsey report in 2024,  
we can see that the development of fashion and digital technology is a trend for the future.  
All companies, whether a supply chain clothing company or a brand,  
need to be timely in the process of digitalization development.  
Keep updating the company’s digital technology,  
keep adapting to digital development,  
so that in the field of clothing technology,  
we can achieve certain breakthroughs or certain results.  

Then the McKinsey report summarizes five trends for us.  
First of all, the first is artificial intelligence and machine learning,  
which is what we have been paying more attention to recently,  
such as deep-seek,  
and then there are 3D and virtual technology,  
VR, AR, and finally blockchain technology.  

Many people also have questions such as,  
the accuracy of 3D design,  
whether we need to do it,  
whether we need to do more practical things,  
and whether we will use different software for different customers,  
and whether 3D design can really replace physical samples,  
and so on.  
There are many questions like this.  

Today I want to discuss these questions with you in depth.  
How should we do it within the company?  
How to adapt to the 3D development trend?  
And then make our own personnel structure more perfect.  

First of all, let’s take a look at the example of a Hugo Boss company.  
As a fashion brand,  
what we really need to do is surprise our customers.  
Our ambition is to become the premium tech-driven fashion platform in the world,  
and 3D can help a lot.  
We have really witnessed a huge transformation,  
but really at Hugo Boss, we started very early with this.  
The designers, the pattern makers,  
everyone is working with 3D software.  
To date, I would say almost four to five hundred people  
are working with those 3D technologies here on the campus.  

The transition from the classic design and classic way of doing things  
to this 3D world has been really tremendous.  
There’s much more room to really think about what we want to do,  
how can we be different this season.  
There are heavy benefits of working 3D end-to-end.  
We have reduced the amount of physical samples that we need to create a collection.  
So teams are actually becoming much more efficient  
and, at the end of the day, creating better products.  

Substance is coming in a very good place.  
It’s helping us to be better digitally and work faster.  
We can really explore creation from scratch.  
For me, working in Substance, it’s super fun.  
Even though I’m not a 3D artist,  
I’m not coming from a 3D school,  
I just learned everything here on the job.  
The design idea gets visual and realistic from the beginning.  
You have endless possibilities.  
With a click of a button I see a color  
that would usually take months or weeks to ship around the globe.  
We have more time to be creative in the design departments  
and, in the end, it’s really good for the environment.  

A key benefit that we’re already seeing today  
is the ability to use 3D also consumer-facing  
and to create media and experiences  
that haven’t been possible  
in classical production processes before.  
A really exciting initiative that we’ve been working on  
called Imaginary Ones,  
where we really collaboratively started to build digital products.  
Really build and create that product that is super relevant  
and that really speaks to that one consumer.  
And with those new communities emerging,  
we have the opportunity to do that.  
And that’s really what this whole transformation is about for us.  

We’re living right now a moment  
which is like when the internet was created.  
Every day is different.  
Every day we have new opportunities and challenges  
or whatever might come up.  
But it’s extremely exciting to witness  
this transformation of the whole industry.  
What is clear to us is that those virtual layers  
will be omnipresent.  
They will raise the way you experience a brand,  
the way you experience a product,  
the way you interact also with brands,  
and it will be much more community-driven.  

Okay, we just finished watching  
Hugo Boss’ presentation  
on the use of 3D virtual technology  
in combination with their own situation.  
In fact, they extended from 3D virtual technology  
to VR, AR, and digital space,  
as well as the metaverse, etc.  
These prerequisites require us to have  
very accurate 3D clothing.  

But for us,  
as a supply chain company,  
why do we use 3D to develop clothing design?  
First of all, from our regular process,  
we design, prepare the fabric, prepare the trims,  
and then review, and then finally approve.  
But many designers, in some cases,  
cannot make definitive choices for their own designs.  
For example, now I have a lot of styles,  
or a lot of fabrics,  
or a lot of patterns,  
or many patterns that cannot be decided,  
which leads to the need for companies  
to make many rounds of physical samples,  
which greatly increases the cost of sampling.  

So after using 3D technology,  
we can show these design solutions in 3D  
in front of us one by one,  
and then replace some of the physical samples  
with 3D clothes.  
In the end, it is very convenient  
to help designers make their own decisions.  
In this case,  
we can save a lot of clothing samples in the early stage.  
And this is the real meaning of 3D design technology.  

But some companies may be ahead in 3D design.  
Some companies are relatively late in 3D design.

First of all,  
the first one is a 3D work made  
based on the understanding of 3D lace fabric  
by some people.  
The latter is the effect  
made after we modified and optimized it.  

So you can clearly see  
that 3D virtual technology  
actually requires in-depth understanding.  
In fact, there is still a lot to understand.

chunks.title: CLO 2025 Academic Month: The Path of 3D Innovation from Concept to Implementation
chunks.content: ## Introduction to 3D Virtual Technology Promotion in Fashion This section introduces the motivation and importance of promoting 3D virtual technology within the fashion supply chain and brands. It highlights key industry trends such as AI, 3D/VR/AR, and blockchain, emphasizing the need for companies to adapt digital technologies to achieve innovation and efficiency. - The development of fashion and digital technology is a major future trend, as highlighted by the 2024 McKinsey report. - Companies in both supply chain and brand sectors must continuously update and adapt to digitalization to achieve breakthroughs in clothing technology. - McKinsey identifies five key trends: artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning, 3D and virtual technology, VR/AR, and blockchain. - Common questions about 3D design include its accuracy, need, software diversity, and whether it can replace physical samples. --- ## Case Study: Hugo Boss and 3D Technology Integration This section details Hugo Boss's early adoption and extensive use of 3D virtual technology in fashion design, illustrating practical benefits and the transformative impact on the design process, sustainability, and customer engagement. - Hugo Boss aims to be a premium tech-driven fashion platform and has integrated 3D technology deeply within its design teams. - Around 400-500 employees work with 3D software, including designers and pattern makers. - The shift from traditional design methods to an end-to-end 3D workflow has increased efficiency, reduced physical sample production, and improved product quality. - The use of Adobe Substance software enables realistic, creative visualization from the design stage, accelerating color and material experimentation. - 3D technology also supports consumer-facing media and experiences, including collaborative digital product initiatives like "Imaginary Ones." - The virtual layer is expected to become omnipresent, enhancing brand interaction and community-driven experiences. --- ## 3D Technology Application in Supply Chain and Design Decision-Making This section explains how supply chain companies use 3D technology to streamline design decisions, reduce physical sampling, and save costs, while emphasizing the importance of accuracy and material understanding in virtual garment creation. - Traditional design processes involve multiple rounds of physical samples due to indecision on styles, fabrics, and patterns, leading to high sampling costs. - 3D technology allows designers to preview virtual garments and make decisions without excessive physical samples. - Comparing two 3D lace fabric renderings demonstrates the necessity of deep understanding of fabric materials, textures, physical properties, and pattern accuracy. - Realistic 3D design requires correct platforms, fabric data, and version control. - Poor 3D renderings (e.g., a lace dress appearing as thick carpet) can harm customer trust and brand perception. - First impressions in 3D presentations are crucial for customer acceptance and confidence. --- ## Best Practices for 3D Design Quality and Team Structure This section provides guidelines for maintaining high-quality 3D design output through standardized processes, skilled personnel, and quality control to build customer trust and facilitate 3D adoption. - Implement a Virtual Quality Standard (VQS) to define a consistent 3D design process including correct platform, fabric data, and version control.

chunks.content: - Poor 3D renderings (e.g., a lace dress appearing as thick carpet) can harm customer trust and brand perception. - First impressions in 3D presentations are crucial for customer acceptance and confidence. --- ## Best Practices for 3D Design Quality and Team Structure This section provides guidelines for maintaining high-quality 3D design output through standardized processes, skilled personnel, and quality control to build customer trust and facilitate 3D adoption. - Implement a Virtual Quality Standard (VQS) to define a consistent 3D design process including correct platform, fabric data, and version control. - Employ Technical Designers (TD) with strong versioning and technical expertise to review and ensure the rationality of 3D versions. - The 3D team should include both technical designers and excellent 3D artists collaborating on a standardized trial process. - Designate a manager responsible for quality control of 3D renderings and public documents to ensure consistent, premium output for customers. - Demonstrated successful 3D trial cases help increase customer confidence and promote wider acceptance of 3D technology. - Early-stage 3D trials have proven effective in reducing sample costs and improving efficiency. --- ## Integration of Advanced Software Tools for Enhanced 3D Effects This section discusses the complementary use of various software such as Substance Designer, Adobe Photoshop, and proprietary tools to achieve superior 3D garment visualizations, including complex materials like bead embroidery and leather. - Combining multiple software tools enhances the realism and detail of 3D designs. - Example: Using CLOUD physical attribute tester data alongside 3D platforms to simulate fabric behavior accurately. - Photoshop assists in refining 3D renders for a more perfect visual outcome. - Substance Designer enables digitization and parameter adjustment of every thread and component, such as color, density, and size. - Realistic effects include reflections on bead embroidery and detailed leather sleeve rendering. - Expanding the software library and combining tools is recommended to optimize 3D presentation quality. --- ## Addressing Inventory and Order Challenges with 3D Technology This section explores how 3D virtual technology can help brands and supply chain companies overcome inventory management challenges and improve product lifecycle and order responsiveness. - Excess inventory globally reached about 5 million units annually in 2023, with a sales value loss of $700,000 to $1.4 million. - Overstock leads to high storage costs, complex management, decreased operational efficiency, and reduced reorders. - Brands are adopting "small orders, fast return" models, involving test orders and rapid market feedback. - 3D technology accelerates design and production of small batches aligned with customer needs, enabling quick market tests and adjustments. - This approach supports healthy product lifecycle management and mitigates storage pressure. - Promoting 3D trials in this context encourages customer acceptance and collaboration. --- ## Synergies Between AI and 3D Technology in Fashion Design This section highlights the integration of AI with 3D design to enhance realism, accelerate workflows, and improve e-commerce presentations. - AI can be combined with 3D models to enhance realism, such as improving wrinkle detail on garments.
